subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP child-session concurrency and fix launch readiness, or intentionally gate rapid distinct ACP spawns for ACPX/Claude until launch is proven safe?
rationale: Current source and tests preserve parallel different-session ACP turns, but the report describes a launch-readiness race where one accepted child never produces output; changing concurrency semantics is a product/runtime policy decision.

options.title: Preserve concurrency, fix readiness
options.body: Run live ACPX/Claude proof and repair the confirmed launch/readiness failure without globally serializing distinct ACP child sessions.

options.title: Gate ACPX/Claude rapid spawns
options.body: Add an explicit, tested ACPX/Claude launch gate or concurrency limit if maintainers prefer reliability over parallel start throughput for this backend.

options.title: Close after live no-repro
options.body: If a current packaged ACPX/Claude two-spawn smoke no longer reproduces, close this as obsolete with the proof transcript.

recommendation.title: Preserve concurrency, fix readiness
recommendation.body: Run live ACPX/Claude proof and repair the confirmed launch/readiness failure without globally serializing distinct ACP child sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The original ACP manager/control-plane and different-session parallel behavior trace to this feature history, making this the best available product-direction owner from code history.
